title: TS-63 Every bot has the computer by default, plus a Pi-style edit tool
description: Decision (user, 2026-10-07): the computer is a basic part of every bot's world. Bots get computer access by default: read_workspace, write_workspace, edit_workspace (new) and run_terminal under /workspace with no per-task grant. (1) Add edit_workspace, a Pi-style exact edit: path, old_text, new_text; replaces exactly one occurrence, fails with a clear message when old_text is missing or ambiguous; runs on the computer through the existing park, claim, regate, result protocol (host-protocol schemas, conversation/src/pi/computer-tools.ts, conversation/src/http/host.ts regate kinds, computer/host/src/executors/workspace.ts), counts as a write for the disk dirty flag, the hydrate-required claim refusal and the live-writer lock. First check whether Pi's own edit implementation (look in node_modules for the pi coding agent package and its tool operations) can be reused against the remote workspace; reuse it if it is a pure function, otherwise implement the same semantics. (2) Change the default turn grant so every bot turn holds these four tools with file scope /workspace (find where the default conversation grant is built; today it is read_workspace and write_workspace only); update the web grant panel logic if it lists tool names (web/lib/turn-grant.ts). The features that state the old default (conversation_turn_grant, conversation_turn_grant_computer, turn_grant_widening, web_turn_grant and others) must change their text on purpose: list every scenario you change. (3) A short bot-facing description: the tool descriptions and the system prompt must tell the model that /workspace is a persistent shared workspace for the organization, that git is available, and to prefer edit_workspace for changes to existing files. Cucumber scenarios first, mutation checks for each group.

comments.text: PR 473 opened, HELD (not merged) until the Pi session handoff spike (branch ts/spike-pi-handoff) reports, per the orchestrator's promise to the user: if sessions run Pi's own tools inside the computer, the remote edit_workspace may be superseded; the default-access change and the model guidance stay useful either way. CI runs on the PR. Ready to merge on the user's word.
